title: Overload: propagate reason codes end-to-end (gateway→routing→runtime) and emit in logs/traces
author: Brian Murphy
release_notes: Hosted API: overload-protected responses now include a stable overload reason code (also emitted to logs and traces) to simplify client retry guidance and incident triage.
description:
Context: As part of Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding, we need a consistent, low-cardinality set of overload reason codes that can be surfaced to (a) customers via the standardized overload error payload and headers, and (b) internal operators via logs/traces/metrics. Today we have multiple ad-hoc “rejected/overloaded” paths across gateway, routing, and runtime, but the reason is either lost entirely or only visible in a single layer’s logs, which makes post-incident analysis and support guidance messy (SUP-3928, SUP-3955). This PR introduces a single canonical OverloadReasonCode enum and plumbs it end-to-end from shed decision to response/logs/traces, without changing the HTTP mapping semantics (those are handled in adr-0147 / ENG-4823).

What’s in this PR (high level): Add a shared enum for overload reason codes: CLOSED/OPEN breaker decisions, edge admission rejections, bounded-queue overflow, memory-pressure shedding, and “client retry storm detected” protections (limited set; see below). Gateway: parse/propagate overload reason from routing/runtime responses and include it in (1) response body field `error.details.overload_reason`, (2) response header `X-Redwood-Overload-Reason`, and (3) structured access log field `overload_reason`. Routing: when returning overload-protected errors (breaker open, capacity shed hint), attach `overload_reason` in the internal response envelope and set trace attribute `redwood.overload_reason`. Runtime: when shedding at scheduler boundaries (queue/prefill/decode) or memory pressure, emit a deterministic `overload_reason` alongside existing shed metrics, and include it in the runtime→routing response metadata. Observability: add trace attribute + log field normalization, plus a small helper to prevent accidental high-cardinality values (only enum values allowed).

Reason code set (v1): EDGE_ADMISSION_DENIED, BREAKER_OPEN, ROUTE_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED, RUNTIME_QUEUE_FULL, RUNTIME_MEMORY_PRESSURE, STREAMING_BACKPRESSURE, SAFETY_RETRY_STORM_GUARD. Notes: (1) these map to a single low-cardinality label set; (2) they are intentionally not model-specific, tenant-specific, or exception-string derived; (3) we can expand later but should treat additions like an API surface change for support + docs.

Implementation details: Added `common/overload/reason_codes.{ts,go,py}` style shared definitions in the monorepo’s shared package `pkg/overload` (Go) and `packages/overload-reasons` (TS) used by gateway and routing. For runtime (Rust), added a mirrored enum with explicit serialization values; routing validates the runtime-provided value against the known set to avoid log injection / unexpected cardinality. Added internal schema field `overload_reason` to the routing response envelope (non-breaking; optional). Gateway maps the field into the external error shape only for overload-protected errors (429/503) so we don’t accidentally expose internal failure detail for true 5xx.

Logging/tracing: Gateway access logs include `overload_reason` only when present and only for overload-protected responses. Routing service logs include `overload_reason` on the request completion log line. Runtime emits `overload_reason` as a field on shed events. Added tracing attributes: `redwood.overload_protected=true|false`, `redwood.overload_reason=<enum>`, and `redwood.breaker_state=open|closed|half_open` (state already existed in some spans; now consistent).

Tests: Unit tests for enum serialization/round-trip in gateway + routing; runtime unit tests for reason selection at queue overflow and memory pressure; a golden test for OpenAI-compat error shape to ensure we don’t break existing clients (the new field is nested under `error.details` and is optional). Added an integration test that simulates runtime queue full and asserts the reason is surfaced at the edge and appears in trace attributes.

Rollout/flags: This change is guarded by the existing overload protection feature flag `overload_protection_v1` (gateway). When disabled, gateway will not emit the header/body field even if upstream includes the reason. Routing/runtime will still attach reasons internally (safe), but only gateway exposure is gated.

Risk assessment: Low-to-medium. Most code paths are additive, but touches multiple services. Main risk is accidental cardinality blowups if we allow free-form reasons; mitigated by strict enum validation at the routing boundary and by disallowing dynamic strings in gateway. Another risk is changing external error payload shape; mitigated by optional fields and OpenAI-compat golden tests.

Follow-ups: (1) Add dashboard panels breaking down shed rate by overload_reason (ENG-4830). (2) SDK surfacing of overload_reason and Retry-After (ENG-4836). (3) Docs update to mention overload reason codes (ENG-4832).

Screenshots/Examples (illustrative): Example header: `X-Redwood-Overload-Reason: RUNTIME_QUEUE_FULL` Example JSON body fragment: `{ "error": { "code": "overloaded", "message": "Service temporarily overloaded", "details": { "overload_reason": "RUNTIME_QUEUE_FULL" } } }`
commits: common(overload): introduce canonical OverloadReasonCode enum + serialization values
routing: attach overload_reason to overload-protected responses and trace attributes
runtime: emit overload_reason for queue-full + memory-pressure shed points
gateway: surface overload_reason in header + error.details and normalize logs
tests: OpenAI-compat golden + integration trace assertions
review_conversation:
Mina Haddad (review): Reason code set looks reasonable, but I’m worried about ROUTE_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED vs BREAKER_OPEN. Are these mutually exclusive? I don’t want customers to see different reasons during the same incident depending on which service answered.

Brian Murphy (author): Agree. In this PR, BREAKER_OPEN is used when breaker is definitively open for (model, region, tier). ROUTE_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED is only used for “soft” shed hints (capacity signal spike) when the breaker is still closed. Added a comment + unit tests in routing to enforce precedence: BREAKER_OPEN > ROUTE_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED.

Amara Diallo (review): Can we ensure we never emit overload_reason for non-overload errors? Specifically, if runtime returns a 500 with some metadata, we must not leak it.

Brian Murphy (author): Yes. Gateway only maps overload_reason into external payload for overload-protected errors (status 429/503 and code=overloaded). For other errors, we drop the field and do not set the header.

Allison Grant (review): Please confirm cardinality is bounded in traces/logs. Also, the trace attribute name should follow our standard prefix.

Brian Murphy (author): Updated attribute names to `redwood.overload_reason` and `redwood.overload_protected` and added validation at routing boundary. If runtime sends an unknown value, we set `overload_reason=UNKNOWN` internally and do not propagate to edge.

Noah Patel (review): Runtime side: STREAMING_BACKPRESSURE seems ambiguous. Is this specifically a shed point? We don’t always “shed” streaming; sometimes we terminate a stream due to upstream cancellation.

Brian Murphy (author): Good catch. I renamed the runtime event mapping so STREAMING_BACKPRESSURE is only set when we proactively disconnect due to overload guardrails (not on client disconnect). Added unit test asserting we do not set it for client-cancel.

Ravi Menon (review): Can you add a minimal integration test proving gateway header propagation? We’ve had regressions where routing metadata was lost.

Brian Murphy (author): Added `integration/overload_reason_propagation_test` that forces runtime queue full, asserts `X-Redwood-Overload-Reason`, and checks trace attributes.

Caleb Johnson (review): CI shows one flake in tracing integration. Can you rerun with increased timeout or make it deterministic?

Brian Murphy (author): Bumped trace export wait from 1s to 3s and added polling with a max deadline; reran CI and it’s stable.

Mina Haddad (approval): LGTM after precedence tests.

Amara Diallo (approval): Approved.

Allison Grant (approval): Approved with naming + cardinality fixes.

Noah Patel (approval): Runtime changes look good.

Ravi Menon (approval): Approved.
